findings.explanation: The controller decides which orders count toward lifetime value by excluding cancelled orders, then sums the order totals itself. That business policy and the resulting total belong in orders.application.

The controller computes each customer's lifetime value with the cancelled-order exclusion, drops customers with zero value, and sorts and ranks them to pick the top N. This is business ranking policy and should be an application-service query.
The controller defines what counts as an active order (status other than cancelled) and uses that to decide which customers have no orders. This business definition belongs in the application layer.
The controller decides that cancelled orders are excluded from units-ordered-per-SKU totals. That business rule about which orders count belongs in an application service, not in the controller.
